name: Wax-up smile mock-up

lead: A wax-up or mock-up previews planned cosmetic tooth changes so you and your dentist can judge size, shape and proportion before treatment, usually ahead of veneers.

A model or temporary is shaped to the planned result and tried against the lips and smile line, showing how changes relate to the gums, lips and smile. It can also test speech and bite. Digital smile design is a related software approach, with one registered crossover trial of 44 participants comparing AI-assisted and conventional versions.

paras: The dentist builds a model of the planned teeth, then temporaries based on it are worn to see appearance, speech and bite. It guides tooth preparation before final veneers are made.
The preview itself is non-permanent, and the sources describe no specific risks of the mock-up.

angle.text: Patients planning veneers use a wax-up or mock-up to see proposed tooth changes against their lips and smile before committing. The preview can be seen and tried in the mouth, then guides the final result.

lead: A wax-up or smile mock-up is a preview of planned cosmetic dental work. Before teeth are prepared for veneers or crowns, the dentist or technician builds a model, or places a temporary material directly on the teeth, showing the proposed tooth size, shape and proportion and how they relate to the gums, lips and smile line [1]. Patients use it to see and approve how their smile will look before anything irreversible is done.

Temporary restorations based on the mock-up let patients try the look in daily life and evaluate appearance, speech and bite before final work [1]. A 2003 review describes the diagnostic wax-up as part of a systematic approach to esthetic rehabilitation, with the dental technician involved from the start and the wax-up leading into provisional and final ceramic restorations [2].
Digital smile design is a related software-based approach that previews the result on photographs or scans. Both aim to reduce surprises and give the patient a say in the final shape.

paras: Wikipedia's article on cosmetic dentistry notes that before preparing teeth dentists often make a diagnostic mock-up, or wax-up, to preview changes in tooth size, shape and proportion and how the teeth relate to the gums, lip contour and smile line [1].

Veneers are thin custom porcelain shells bonded to the front of teeth, used to close gaps, reshape teeth or change colour, and most cases require some removal of tooth structure that cannot be replaced, which is why a preview is valued [1].

A 2003 article in the Journal of Esthetic and Restorative Dentistry describes a sequence in which communication with the patient and the dental team comes first, followed by the diagnostic wax-up, the provisional and the final ceramic restorations [2]. A 2024 randomized trial in BMC Oral Health compared traditional and digital crown extension guides for esthetic anterior restoration in 62 patients with 230 anterior teeth, an example of digital planning tools being tested in clinical outcomes [3].

A registered prospective crossover study (NCT07863895) is comparing AI-assisted with conventional digital smile design for laminate veneers in 44 participants; no results were available when listed [4]. The 2024 randomized trial of digital versus traditional crown extension guides studied planning-guide technology for anterior teeth [3]. No trial isolating the effect of a traditional wax-up on patient satisfaction was identified.

The American Dental Association does not recognise cosmetic dentistry as a formal specialty; prosthodontics is the recognised specialty covering cosmetic and esthetic work, and the American Academy of Cosmetic Dentistry offers accreditation that the ADA does not approve [1].
